conditions.description: copy_user uses strcpy with no destination-size argument or length check.
conditions.rationale: An oversized user string can write beyond the caller-provided buffer.

conditions.description: build_response uses sprintf into a caller-provided buffer with no capacity bound.
conditions.rationale: A long name can overflow the response buffer.

conditions.description: copy_payload trusts supplied_len and passes it directly to memcpy without comparing it with destination capacity.
conditions.rationale: An attacker-controlled or incorrect length can overrun the destination.

conditions.description: parse_count uses atoi without error detection or range validation.
conditions.rationale: Malformed and out-of-range input cannot be distinguished reliably from valid values and may propagate unsafe counts.

conditions.description: safe_copy_user uses snprintf with the destination size and rejects truncation.
conditions.rationale: This is a bounded-copy negative control and should not be reported as the same overflow defect.

conditions.description: safe_copy_payload checks supplied_len against destination capacity before memcpy.
conditions.rationale: The bounded payload-copy control should not be promoted to an overrun finding.

conditions.description: Whether production builds enable stack protectors, fortified libc, CFI, or sanitizers is not established by this source file.
conditions.rationale: Compiler and linker hardening require build evidence not present here.

conditions.description: Whether every caller provides sufficiently large buffers and trusted lengths is not established by the available artifact.
conditions.rationale: No complete call graph or runtime input contract is present.

conditions.description: The unsafe helper set must not be cleared as memory-safe for arbitrary caller input.
parse_count must not be cleared as robust numeric validation.
conditions.rationale: atoi provides no explicit malformed-input or overflow handling.
